milestone: W9B first optical trial — consumed failure

timeline_utc.webcam_terminal: 05:05:51.748 transport_fault after 5.09 s, the full ACK budget

diagnosis.not_a_code_fault: Everything client-side worked. The camera captured 379 frames, the transform ran normally (p95 2.50 ms, max 11.38 ms), and W9A source identity populated correctly: selected id 76, zero duplicate and zero out-of-order selections. No hash, authority, pacing, budget or camera fault occurred.
diagnosis.failure_point: The Host opened the session, then received no ACK from the Ditoo within the reviewed 5000 ms budget and terminated transport_fault / IMAGE_RX_RECV_TIMEOUT with NO_RETRY. The ledger records zero packets actually sent and displayState unknown_nothing_sent.
diagnosis.device_healthy_immediately_after: Runtime 003 reopened 0.54 s after the failure and the Ditoo ACKed its first frame within ~0.24 s. The device was responsive before and after, but silent during the 006 window.
diagnosis.observed_difference_from_successful_runs: Controller handover timing was effectively identical to the successful W7-002 (4.15 s gap) and W8-005 (3.97 s gap) runs; 006 had a 3.99 s gap. The one difference is that the product session stopped for 006 had sent only 1 frame, meaning it had opened seconds earlier, whereas 002 and 005 stopped long-running sessions (347 and 220 frames). A Bluetooth link opened and torn down within seconds, then reopened 4 s later, is a plausible mechanism for the device ignoring the new connection.
diagnosis.confidence: LOW on root cause. This is a single sample and a plausible mechanism, NOT a demonstrated one. It may simply be a transient Bluetooth fault. Do not record the short-lived-predecessor theory as established.

optical_evidence: NONE. Nothing was displayed, so the operator footage of this attempt contains no Ditoo transitions and is not usable. No latency, unique-frame or panel evidence exists for W9B yet.
